National Geographic в Instagram : "Living on the steepest street in the continental United States comes with some uphill battles—from icy winter commutes to runaway trash cans.
 
Michael Hartman, a certified first responder who has lived on Canton Avenue, in Pittsburgh's Beechview neighborhood, for five years, has been known to administer first aid to the cyclists who regularly test their mettle on the climb during an annual race.
 
With a maximum grade of 37 percent, Canton is not the kind of street you leisurely stroll—or bike—up.

In recognition of the 250th anniversary of U.S. independence, we're celebrating the grandest, wildest, and strangest bits of American geography and culture across every state and territory.

Explore more Wonders of America at the link in bio.

Video by @david_s_allee"

National Geographic в Instagram : "In 2025, Kazi and 15 other cheetahs undertook a grueling 53-hour translocation from South Africa to Mozambique—the largest cheetah relocation ever attempted. Such a journey can be risky, but it's necessary to ensure the survival of a species with fewer than 7,100 individuals remaining worldwide, both in the wild and in captivity. After navigating bureaucracy, torrential rain, and a car crash, the effort has proven initially successful one year on, with Kazi giving birth to these three cubs.

Following the journey of the largest cheetah relocation attempted at the link in bio. 

Video by Slots Media and @theoriginsfoundation."

National Geographic в Instagram : "For the first time in more than 900 years, the Bayeux Tapestry—a 225-foot-long work of medieval art depicting the Norman Conquest of England—has arrived in the U.K. Transporting one of the world's most famous and fragile antiquities meant navigating numerous practical and political hurdles and required years of planning, with conservators and engineers developing a highly specialized process to protect the tapestry. 
 
Nat Geo writer Chris Heath and photographer @zed_nelson witnessed its arrival at the British Museum in London in the early hours of July 10, marking an accomplishment that many considered impossible. 

Learn more about the secret mission to move the world's most famous tapestry at the link in bio."

National Geographic в Instagram : "Humans kill millions of sharks each year, and overfishing poses a major threat to their populations—especially hammerheads, since they grow and reproduce slowly. These iconic creatures are already at the brink of extinction, but successful marine protection initiatives offer a glimpse of hope for the future. 

#HammerheadSharksUpClose with @bertiegregory is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu."

National Geographic в Instagram : "Rank America's 63 national parks by size, and Great Smoky Mountains comes in middling. But scientists have identified a stunning range of some 23,000 species there, famously including more salamander varieties than anyplace else on Earth. 

See more Wonders of America at the link in bio.

Video by @bystephanievermillion"

National Geographic в Instagram : "Is this the cutest mealtime you’ve ever seen? These meerkat pups are fueling up with mom. As they grow, the clan will help the matriarch raise the next generation—a cooperative way of life that’s becoming more important as the Kalahari grows hotter and drier. 

Learn why powerful matriarchs are vital to meerkat survival at the link in bio. 

Video by @ottowhitehead"

National Geographic в Instagram : "The timespan of an iceberg is usually measured in years, not decades. A23a was different. For forty years, the world's largest iceberg endured in a changing ocean, quietly shedding itself in the background as humanity slowly began to experience the consequences of a warming world. Simultaneously remarkable and ignored, A23a only achieved fame near the end, when it arrived in open water. Suddenly accessible to both scientists and tourists, its last days were witnessed by people who marveled at its size even as it crumbled and diminished before their eyes. This surreal, surprising behemoth is mostly gone now, but the lessons it taught humanity, both scientific and intangible, remain.

Discover more about the extraordinary legacy of the world's largest iceberg at the link in bio."

National Geographic в Instagram : "Don't let their size fool you. Elephants are as graceful as they are massive. 🐘 @joelsartore has so many reasons to love elephants—what's your favorite thing about them?

We’re celebrating 20 years of the National Geographic #PhotoArk, an audacious project documenting the world's incredible biodiversity and highlighting the importance of conservation through photography. Which animal do you want to see next?"

National Geographic в Instagram : "Instead of going in for the kill, this mother orca spins the sea turtle, holds it beneath the surface, and drags it by the flipper as her calf watches on. Researchers examining this footage captured in the Gulf of California believe it may be evidence of teaching, rather than an orca simply playing with her food—especially since orca calves spend a great deal of time by their mothers' side during their infancy.

Find out more about how animals share survival lessons at the link in bio. 

Video by Alonso I. Rodríguez de la Parra/Mares de Mexico."

National Geographic в Instagram : "Some sharks navigate across entire ocean basins, covering distances comparable to Earth's circumference. Hidden within their snouts is the sensory system that helps guide these extraordinary journeys. But some species are adjusting their migrations—National Geographic Explorer Arzucan Askin (@zuzu_askin) explains why."
